title: Procurement: Legal Review Triage & Escalation SOP
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
This SOP sets out how Redwood Inference triages procurement items that need legal review or escalation to other functions. It is meant to shorten cycle times, keep contracting and billing risk under control, and make ownership and review SLAs clear for each tier.

Scope
- Covers vendor engagements, SOWs, license purchases, hardware leases (including GPU reservations), SaaS subscriptions and professional services agreements raised through Procurement.
- Does not cover low-value purchases made under the corporate purchasing card (P-card) policy (see /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/p-card-guidelines).

Definitions
1) Low-risk procurement: under <$10k, no data access, standard market terms, no cross-border data transfer.
2) Medium-risk procurement: $10k–$250k, limited non-sensitive data access, or limited bespoke terms (payment schedules, warranty clarifications).
3) High-risk procurement: >$250k, access to customer data or models, on-prem or network connectivity, escrow/KMS requirements, indemnity/limitation clause changes, or vendor-requested data residency exceptions.
4) Contracting Owner: the Procurement lead assigned to the purchase.
5) Legal Triage Owner: the commercial counsel doing the initial review.

Decision Matrix (quick reference)
| Value band | Data access | Special clauses requested | Initial path | SLA (initial review) | Escalation
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| <$10k | None | Standard T&C | Procurement approval | 2 business days | Procurement Manager
| <$10k | Non-sensitive | Minor clarifications | Procurement + Legal FYI | 3 business days | Legal (if changes requested)
| $10k–$250k | Non-sensitive | Payment / warranty edits | Legal triage | 5 business days | Senior Counsel
| >$250k or any sensitive data | Any | Any bespoke confidentiality / KMS / escrow | Legal + Security + Finance | 10 business days | GC + Head of Procurement + Security

Procedure (step-by-step)
1. Intake
   a. The requestor raises a PR in the Procurement system (Jira/Workday) with the vendor quote, SOW, standard T&C and vendor risk questionnaire attached.
   b. The Procurement Owner assigns a risk band and a Contracting Owner.
2. Procurement pre-checks
   a. Confirm the vendor is on the approved vendor list and KYC is complete.
   b. Run the third-party risk scan and attach the report.
3. Legal triage (Commercial Counsel)
   a. Three-part review: (1) material exposures (indemnity, liability caps, warranty, IP, data access); (2) billing and rev-rec implications (checklist below); (3) standard redlines.
   b. Use Clause Library templates for common items (data transfer addendum, limited indemnity, software license grant).
4. Cross-functional review (when required)
   a. Security: needed for network connectivity, data access, KMS/escrow or on-prem deployments. The Security lead signs off within 5 business days of assignment.
   b. Finance: needed for unusual billing cadence, revenue-sharing or subscription changes; confirms revenue recognition and billing trigger alignment.
   c. Product/Platform: confirms technical SOW accuracy and operational acceptance criteria for managed services.
5. Negotiation & approval
   a. Procurement negotiates commercial terms; Legal negotiates legal language.
   b. High-risk contracts need final sign-off from Head of Procurement, Commercial Counsel and Director of Finance.
6. Execution & post-signature
   a. File the executed contract in DocuSign + ContractDB with the metadata below.
   b. Kick off supplier onboarding: finance (AP routing), security (vulnerability scan), ops (service acceptance).

Contract Metadata (ContractDB required fields)
- contract_id: Redwood identifier (e.g., RDW-CTR-2025-000087)
- vendor_legal_name
- purchasing_owner: "team/person"
- commercial_owner: "Procurement lead"
- legal_owner: "Commercial counsel"
- start_date / end_date / renewal_terms
- not_to_exceed_value / committed_spend_line_items
- billing_trigger: invoicing cadence and the rev-rec triggering event
- data_classification_and_controls: none | non-sensitive | regulated | restricted
- kyc_status: complete | incomplete
- escrow_or_kms_required: yes | no
- confidentiality: internal | restricted | customer-only
- signed_copy_link: internal storage URL

Revenue Recognition & Billing Checklist (Finance, before legal approval)
- Identify each performance obligation and its billing trigger (API access vs. physical hardware delivery).
- Check whether the contract shifts revenue timing (advance payments, non-refundable fees, milestone billing).
- Align invoicing cadence with subscription terms, e.g.:
  Example 1: Monthly subscription — billed in arrears on the 1st of the following month; revenue recognized ratably over the month.
  Example 2: Annual prepay — billed at execution; revenue recognized ratably over 12 months.
  Example 3: Hardware + installation SOW — hardware recognized at delivery; installation recognized over the acceptance period.

Service Level Targets for Reviews
- Procurement intake validation: 1 business day.
- Legal initial triage: 2–10 business days by band.
- Security review when required: 5 business days.
- Negotiated contract to signature: medium-risk target 15 business days; high-risk target 30 business days.

Escalation Contacts
- Procurement Manager: Maya Thompson — procurement@redwoodinference.com — intake issues.
- Legal: Diego Morales — diego.morales@redwoodinference.com — commercial counsel.
- Senior Counsel / GC: Eleanor West — eleanor.west@redwoodinference.com — policy exceptions.
- Finance RevRec: Priya Singh — priya.singh@redwoodinference.com — billing/revrec edge cases.
- Security: Jin Park — jin.park@redwoodinference.com — data and network escalations.

Exception Handling & Emergency Procurement
- Emergency purchases (e.g., critical hardware replacement) can be approved by Head of Procurement + Head of Finance with legal review after the fact. Record the rationale and finish a post-facto risk assessment within 5 business days.
- Multi-year commitments with budget impact must be coordinated with Budget Owners and FP&A for the next forecast cycle.

Template Clauses
1) Limitation of Liability (recommended cap): "Except for willful misconduct or breach of confidentiality, liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) USD 500,000 or (ii) the fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim."
2) DPA pointer: "Attach the DPA in Appendix A; vendor must support EU SCCs and document KMS integration for customer-managed keys where required."
3) Escrow/KMS: "Where customer datasets or model weights in on-prem or model-hosting arrangements may be subject to e-discovery or regulatory requests, vendor must provide an escrow arrangement or KMS integration documented in Schedule 3."

Audit & Reporting Requirements
- Quarterly compliance report to Finance and Legal: executed contracts > $100k and any SOP deviations.
- Monthly aging report of contracts in negotiation by risk band.
- Post-mortem for high-risk negotiations that ran past 30 business days.

Appendix A: Legal Redline Checklist
- IP ownership and license grants.
- Indemnity and open-source carve-outs.
- Limitation of liability and insurance obligations.
- Confidentiality duration and return/destruction.
- Termination for convenience and transition assistance.

Appendix B: Tagging a contract in ContractDB
$ contractdb tag add --id RDW-CTR-2025-000087 --label "data:non-sensitive" --field billing_trigger="monthly_in_arrears" --owner procurement/maya.thompson

- Contract clause library: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-clause-library-2025

Owners & Maintenance

- Steward: Commercial Counsel (Diego Morales).
- Reviewed annually or on material policy change.

This SOP is the governing procedure for procurement legal triage and escalation; deviations require a documented exception approved by the GC and Head of Finance.
